# Verdict: REVISE ## Overall Assessment The component correctly implements individual radio button semantics (labels, `name` grouping, `checked` state) but **fails to semantically group the radio set**. The group label is a presentational `
` with zero programmatic association to the inputs. Screen reader users hear individual options with no context for what they are choosing. Additionally, the hardcoded `name="options"` creates a collision risk across component instances. ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, I predicted: 1. **Missing `
`/``** — the group label would be a plain `
` with no programmatic link to the radios. ✅ Confirmed. 2. **No `role="radiogroup"` fallback** — no ARIA alternative provided. ✅ Confirmed. 3. **Hardcoded `name` attribute** — collision risk with multiple instances. ✅ Confirmed. 4. **Arrow-key navigation** — I expected this might be missing, but native HTML handles it via the `name` attribute. ❌ Not an issue (native behavior covers it). 5. **Missing `aria-describedby` for helper text** — no helper text exists in this component, so N/A. ## Critical Findings (blocks access) None. The user can still select a radio option; the gap is contextual, not a total access block. ## Major Findings (significantly degrades experience) ### 1. Radio group lacks semantic grouping — group name invisible to assistive technology **Evidence:** `BuggyRadioGroup.jsx`, lines 8–9 ```jsx
{label}
``` The group label is rendered as a `
` with a CSS class. It has **no programmatic relationship** to the `` elements. There is no `
`, no ``, no `role="radiogroup"`, no `aria-label`, and no `aria-labelledby`. **User group impacted:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) **What the user experiences:** - A sighted user sees: *"Choose your plan: ○ Basic ○ Pro ○ Enterprise"* - A screen reader user hears: *"Basic, radio button, not checked. Pro, radio button, not checked. Enterprise, radio button, not checked."* The group name ("Choose your plan") is **never announced**. The user must infer the purpose from the option text alone. If options are opaque ("Option A", "Option B"), the user has zero context. **WCAG / APG citation:** - **WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships):** "Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text." The label-to-group relationship is conveyed only visually. - **WAI-ARIA APG — Radio Group pattern:** "The container element must have `role='radiogroup'` and an accessible name." The native HTML equivalent is `
` + ``. - **WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value):** The group must expose its name to assistive technology. **Confidence:** HIGH **Fix (preferred — native HTML):** ```jsx
{label} {options.map((option) => ( ))}
``` **Fix (alternative — ARIA, if `
` is structurally impossible):** ```jsx
{options.map((option) => ( ))}
``` Per the non-negotiable rule: **native HTML (`
`/``) is the correct choice here.** ARIA `role="radiogroup"` is only acceptable when `
` cannot be used (e.g., inside a `` where `
` is invalid). --- ### 2. Hardcoded `name="options"` creates cross-instance collision **Evidence:** `BuggyRadioGroup.jsx`, line 15 ```jsx name="options" ``` The `name` attribute is a string literal. If two instances of `BuggyRadioGroup` render on the same page (e.g., "Choose plan" and "Choose billing cycle"), they share the same `name`. Selecting a radio in one group **deselects** the radio in the other group. **User group impacted:** All users (functional bug), but especially screen reader and keyboard users who rely on the group semantics to understand which set they're interacting with. **WCAG / APG citation:** - **WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships):** The `name` attribute defines the radio group. A collision breaks the relationship. - **WCAG 3.2.1 (On Focus):** Focusing a radio in one group unexpectedly changes state in another group is an unexpected context change. **Confidence:** HIGH **Fix:** ```jsx const BuggyRadioGroup = ({ label, options = [], name, id }) => { // ... }; ``` The parent must supply a unique `name` (or `id`) per instance. This is a **required prop** in the component's contract. --- ## Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) - **No `disabled` or `required` prop passthrough:** The component doesn't accept or forward `disabled`, `required`, or `aria-describedby` props. If a parent needs to mark the group as required or attach a description, there's no mechanism. (WCAG 3.3.2 — Labels in Context.) - **No `onChange` callback prop:** The component manages state internally with `useState` but exposes no `onChange` to the parent. This is a design limitation, not strictly an a11y issue, but it prevents the parent from announcing selection changes via a live region. (WCAG 4.1.3 — Status Messages.) ## Enhancements (best practice not met) - **Add `aria-describedby` support:** Allow a `description` prop that renders helper text and associates it via `aria-describedby` on each radio (or on the `
`). This helps cognitive users understand constraints (e.g., "Pro plan includes up to 10 team members"). - **Consider `role="radiogroup"` + `aria-labelledby` if the label is a separate element:** If the visual label must remain a sibling (not a ``), use `aria-labelledby` pointing to the label's `id` to create the programmatic association. ## What's Missing (gaps) | Gap | Why it matters | |-----|---------------| | `
` / `` (or `role="radiogroup"` + accessible name) | Screen reader users cannot determine what the group is for | | Unique `name` per instance | Multiple groups on a page break each other; AT announces conflicting groupings | | `aria-describedby` support | No way to attach helper text or error messages to the group | | `onChange` / `onSelect` callback | Parent cannot announce selection changes to a live region (WCAG 4.1.3) | | `required` / `disabled` prop passthrough | No way to communicate required state or disable the group programmatically | ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Assessment | |-------------|-------------|------------| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | Group name is invisible. User hears isolated radio buttons with no context. The core semantic relationship (label → group) is absent. This is the primary failure. | | **Keyboard-only** | LOW | Native HTML handles arrow-key navigation within the radio group via the `name` attribute. Tab enters the group, arrows cycle, Tab leaves. No issue. | | **Low vision** | LOW | The visual label is present. At 200% zoom, the layout reflows (assuming standard CSS). No code-level concern. | | **Cognitive** | MEDIUM | Without the group name announced, a user who relies on AT must infer purpose from option text. Helper text (`aria-describedby`) is not supported. | | **Vestibular & motion** | LOW | No animations, transitions, or auto-playing content. Not relevant. | | **Auditory access** | LOW | No media elements. Not relevant. | | **Environmental contrast** | LOW | No inline styles or color-dependent state indicators in the code. Contrast is a CSS concern outside this component. | ## Verdict Justification **REVISE** — The component has one MAJOR semantic gap (missing group name for AT) and one MAJOR functional/a11y bug (hardcoded `name`). Neither blocks access entirely (the user can still select a radio), but the screen reader experience is significantly degraded: the user cannot determine what they are choosing. The fix is straightforward — replace `
`/`
` with `
`/`` and parameterize the `name` attribute. **To upgrade to ACCEPT:** 1. Wrap the radio inputs in `
` with a `` containing the `label` prop. 2. Accept a unique `name` (or `id`) prop and use it on the `` elements. 3. (Recommended) Add `aria-describedby` support for helper text. **To upgrade to ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS:** - If `
` is structurally impossible in the parent layout, `role="radiogroup"` + `aria-label={label}` is an acceptable ARIA fallback. Document the reason. ## Open Questions (unscored) - **Is this component ever rendered inside a `
`?** If so, `
` is invalid HTML inside `
`, and `role="radiogroup"` becomes the correct choice. This changes the recommended fix. - **Is the `label` prop always a simple string?** If it can be a React node (e.g., `Choose plan`), then `` is still correct, but `aria-label` (string-only) would not work — `aria-labelledby` with an `id` would be needed. - **Are there validation/error states planned?** If so, the component needs `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` wiring now, not retrofitted later. ## Self-Audit Summary | Finding | Confidence | Refutable? | Gap or Preference? | |---------|-----------|------------|--------------------| | Missing fieldset/legend | HIGH | No — code clearly uses `
` | GAP | | Hardcoded `name` | HIGH | No — literal string in source | GAP | | No `aria-describedby` support | MEDIUM | Yes — may be out of scope for v1 | GAP (minor) | | No `onChange` callback | MEDIUM | Yes — design choice | PREFERENCE (noted as enhancement) | No findings were downgraded or moved to Open Questions. No findings were manufactured. The two MAJOR findings are unambiguous from the source code.
